input_messages.content: Hi there! I’m having trouble sending MMS messages from my phone. It’s been happening for the past few hours, and I’d really like to get it working again. Can you help me figure out what’s going on?
Sure! My name is John Smith, and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know what you need me to do next.
I checked, and my messaging app currently cannot send MMS messages. What should I try next?
Looking at my phone’s status bar, I see one bar for signal strength (so the signal is poor), it says 2G, and mobile data is enabled. Airplane Mode is not on. What should I do next?
I changed my network mode to “4G/5G preferred,” and now my status bar shows excellent signal strength and 5G is active. Should I try sending an MMS again now?
I tried again, but my messaging app still can’t send MMS messages. Is there something else I should check or try?
I checked my APN settings. The APN name is set to "internet," and the MMSC URL is "http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc." Both settings appear to be filled in. What should I do next?
I checked, and Wi-Fi Calling is already turned off on my phone. What should I try next?
I checked my messaging app’s permissions, and it only has permission for “phone.” It doesn’t have permissions for storage or SMS. Should I go ahead and enable those permissions?
I’ve enabled both the “Storage” and “SMS” permissions for my messaging app. I checked again, and now it looks like I can send MMS messages! Thank you for your help—everything seems to be working now.
Thank you so much for your help and patience! I appreciate the step-by-step guidance. Everything’s working perfectly now. Have a wonderful day! ###STOP###

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?
Hi there! I’m having trouble sending MMS messages from my phone. It’s been happening for the past few hours, and I’d really like to get it working again. Can you help me figure out what’s going on?

I can help you troubleshoot your MMS issue. To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth,
- Or your customer ID?

Once I have this information, I can begin assisting you.
Sure! My name is John Smith, and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know what you need me to do next.

Thank you for providing your information. To help you with your MMS issue, I’ll need you to perform a few quick checks on your phone. 

First, could you please check if you can send MMS messages using your messaging app? If your phone has a diagnostic tool or option to "check if you can send MMS," please use it and let me know the result.

If you’re not sure how to do this, let me know, and I’ll guide you through the steps!
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I checked, and my messaging app currently cannot send MMS messages. What should I try next?

Thank you for checking. Since your messaging app cannot send MMS messages, let’s go through some troubleshooting steps. 

First, let’s make sure your phone has cellular service and mobile data enabled, as both are required for MMS. Could you please check your phone’s status bar and let me know:
- If you see any signal bars (indicating cellular service)
- If mobile data is enabled (look for 4G, 5G, LTE, or similar icons)
- If Airplane Mode is on

If you’re unsure how to check these, I can guide you through the process. Let me know what you see!
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Looking at my phone’s status bar, I see one bar for signal strength (so the signal is poor), it says 2G, and mobile data is enabled. Airplane Mode is not on. What should I do next?

Thank you for the details. Since your phone is connected to a 2G network, this could be the reason why MMS is not working—MMS generally requires at least a 3G connection.

Please change your network mode preference to allow your phone to connect to 4G or 5G networks if available. Look for an option in your phone’s settings called “Network Mode” or “Preferred Network Type,” and select “4G/5G preferred” or a similar option.

Once you’ve done this, check if your signal improves and try sending an MMS again. Let me know if you need step-by-step instructions for changing your network mode.

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
I changed my network mode to “4G/5G preferred,” and now my status bar shows excellent signal strength and 5G is active. Should I try sending an MMS again now?

Yes, please try sending an MMS message now that your phone is connected to a 5G network with excellent signal strength. 

Let me know if the MMS goes through successfully or if you still encounter any issues.
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I tried again, but my messaging app still can’t send MMS messages. Is there something else I should check or try?

Thank you for letting me know. Since you now have excellent signal and 5G, but MMS still isn’t working, the next step is to check your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings, as incorrect APN settings are a common cause of MMS issues.

Please check your APN settings and specifically look for the MMSC (Multimedia Messaging Service Center) URL. If you see that the APN or MMSC URL is missing or incorrect, let me know. If you’re unsure how to check this, I can guide you through the process. 

Once you’ve checked, please let me know what you find.

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)
I checked my APN settings. The APN name is set to "internet," and the MMSC URL is "http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc." Both settings appear to be filled in. What should I do next?

Thank you for checking your APN settings and confirming that both the APN name and MMSC URL are set. The next step is to check if Wi-Fi Calling is enabled on your device, as this can sometimes interfere with MMS functionality.

Please check your phone’s settings to see if Wi-Fi Calling is turned ON. If it is, please turn it OFF and then try sending an MMS message again.

Let me know if Wi-Fi Calling was enabled and if turning it off resolves the issue. If it was already off, please let me know as well.
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned OFF.
I checked, and Wi-Fi Calling is already turned off on my phone. What should I try next?

Thank you for confirming that Wi-Fi Calling is off. The next step is to check if your messaging app has the necessary permissions to send MMS messages, specifically access to storage and SMS.

Please check your messaging app’s permissions in your phone’s settings and ensure that both “Storage” and “SMS” permissions are granted. If either is missing, please enable them.

Let me know if you find any missing permissions and if granting them allows you to send MMS. If both permissions are already enabled, please let me know.
The following apps are installed on the phone: messaging, browser
App 'messaging' has permission for: phone.
I checked my messaging app’s permissions, and it only has permission for “phone.” It doesn’t have permissions for storage or SMS. Should I go ahead and enable those permissions?

Yes, please enable both “Storage” and “SMS” permissions for your messaging app. These permissions are required for sending and receiving MMS messages.

After granting these permissions, try sending an MMS message again and let me know if it works.

Success. Permission 'storage' granted to app 'messaging'.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Success. Permission 'sms' granted to app 'messaging'.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app can send MMS messages.
I’ve enabled both the “Storage” and “SMS” permissions for my messaging app. I checked again, and now it looks like I can send MMS messages! Thank you for your help—everything seems to be working now.
I’m glad to hear that enabling the necessary permissions resolved your MMS issue! If you have any more questions or need further assistance in the future, feel free to reach out. Have a great day!
